items.note: Every capability bullet under New Capabilities names a kebab-case path (segments separated by '/').

sources.quote: Use kebab-case for path segments you introduce (e.g., user-auth or identity/user-auth) ... - `<capability-path>`: <brief description of what this capability covers>

items.note: Spotting runtime context or guidance text copied into files would need a fingerprint of that text. No such fingerprint is defined, so no kind can check this.

sources.quote: Do not copy runtime context or operation guidance into implementation files or planning artifacts

items.note: Telling whether a capability name is an implementation task is a judgment about meaning. The full list of proposal section names cannot be cited, so a literal disjointness check is not grounded.

sources.quote: Do not name implementation tasks or proposal sections.

items.note: This needs each listed capability path mapped to openspec/specs/<path>/spec.md in base_paths. Selectors cannot do that mapping, and the 'Modified Capabilities' heading text is not in the cited lines.

sources.quote: Use the exact existing path under openspec/specs/.

items.note: .openspec.yaml is not an artifact with selectors, so the skip_specs marker under the 'no capabilities' condition cannot be checked.

sources.quote: A change with no capabilities at all (pure refactor, tooling, docs) must set `skip_specs: true` in its .openspec.yaml

unitemized.reason: This only allows Modified Capabilities to be empty when no requirement changes. Whether requirements changed is a judgment call that no predicate can observe.
